sp.name: Swept path
sp.numbers: Everything here is a planning aid. The engineer decides: a result is not a certificate, a stamped design or a statement that a vehicle can or cannot use a road. No dynamics, braking, speed or driver behaviour is modelled, only low-speed geometry.
sp.privacy: Your project stays on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.
sp.uncited: Figures with no source named in the pack: {list}.
sp.pdf.title: Swept path report
sp.placeholder: UNVERIFIED placeholder figures. Set the vehicle from the design vehicle your jurisdiction requires (copy it below, edit it) before relying on a result.
sp.veh.help: A vehicle is a small JSON description in metres and degrees. Change the figures, then save: the copy is yours, named my-…, and is always marked unverified until you check it.
sp.err.nopath: Pick an alignment or a line with at least two points first.
sp.err.norun: Run a vehicle along a path first.
sp.err.noboundary: Draw a closed line for the lot first, then press Refresh.
sp.err.roadonly: This check needs a road vehicle.
sp.run.help: A road vehicle or an aircraft's nose gear follows the path with its front axle; reversing follows with the last axle. A light rail car keeps both bogies on the track.
sp.r.swing: Body swing off the track at the middle
sp.stamped: {n} lines drawn into the project (one undo step).
sp.obs.none: There are no lines or parcels in the project to check against.
sp.clr.help: Tick what the vehicle must not touch, set a margin, and check the last run. Each conflict becomes a Problem you can jump to.
sp.clr.hit: {n} obstacles are touched or closer than the margin.
sp.issue.conflict: {v} comes within {d} {u} of {name} at {s} {u} along the path.
sp.issue.steer: {v} needs a steering angle of {value} degrees; its lock is {limit}.
sp.issue.short: The path is too short to run {v}.
sp.issue.hitch: A trailer hitch of {v} is ahead of the axle; it is taken as on the axle.
sp.rb.help: Draw a roundabout from a circle, a lane and its legs, then run every entry and exit of the chosen road vehicle through it. The movements are smoothed paths; the island is the only obstacle checked.
sp.rb.legs: Leg angles in degrees (0 = east, counter-clockwise)
sp.rb.note: Steering angles over the lock and rides over the island are marked. A roundabout also needs sight distance and entry deflection checks; this does not do them.
sp.pk.help: Lay out bays and an aisle inside a closed line, count them, and check how the chosen vehicle pulls into the hardest bay with its neighbours occupied.
sp.pk.double: Bays on both sides of the aisle
sp.pk.cap: Only the first {n} bays are drawn.
sp.pk.nobays: No bay fits: make the lot larger or the bays smaller.
sp.pk.fine: The vehicle pulls into the hardest bay without touching its neighbours and inside its steering lock.
sp.pk.trouble: {n} neighbouring bays are touched and {p} steering or articulation limits are reached.
sp.pk.note: The hardest bay is the last one in the last row. The path is a smoothed turn from the aisle; a real driver may do better or worse.
